what_it_is: API security vendor with AI Gateway for agent containment, MCP governance and runtime guardrails.
identity_note: Cequence Security (cequence.ai). Scope: AI Gateway, Agent Personas, AI Discovery and Unified API Protection.

1.reason: AI Discovery maps shadow agents, MCP servers and LLM providers from SIEM logs only.
1.evidence: It surfaces every shadow MCP server, agent, and LLM provider enterprise-wide from existing SIEM logs.
1.has: AI Discovery in AI Gateway inventories shadow agents, MCP servers and LLMs.
1.lacks: No cloud AI asset inventory, shadow AI on endpoints or AI pipeline posture.

2.reason: AI Gateway discovers, registers and polices MCP servers. Persona limits tool calls but no sandbox.
2.evidence: Agent Personas scope every agent to the tools, APIs, skills, and LLMs its job requires
2.has: MCP registry, Agent Personas and Agent Behavior Protection in Cequence AI Gateway.
2.lacks: No host sandbox. Only a Copilot Studio demo, no managed platform connectors.

3.reason: Agent Behavior Protection scores sessions and halts off-task agents. Audit events export to Splunk and Datadog.
3.evidence: You can forward audit events to your existing SIEM or observability platform.
3.has: Behavior analysis on gateway sessions. SIEM export to Splunk, Datadog, OTLP and syslog.
3.lacks: No cloud control-plane log detection. Blocks tool calls, not hosts.

4.reason: Prompt Guard blocks injection and DLP redacts or blocks sensitive data in requests and responses.
4.evidence: Prompt Guard detects prompt injection, override instructions, and safety filter bypass attempts before they reach a model or tool.
4.has: Prompt Guard, system prompt lock and 100+ DLP detection types at the gateway.
4.lacks: No browser extension. No toxicity, hallucination or code output filtering found.

5.reason: Per-tool-call audit records export to SIEM. Controls mapped to OWASP agentic Top 10 in blog.
5.evidence: Mapping Cequence AI Gateway Controls to OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications
5.has: Audit trail, OWASP agentic mapping and EU AI Act evidence page for AI Gateway.
5.lacks: No AIBOM export. Framework mapping sits in blogs, not in product reports.

6.reason: Cequence positions AI Gateway as runtime containment and lists no red team product.
6.evidence: Searches: Cequence red teaming AI agents testing, Cequence AI gateway adversarial testing OR red team OR simulate attacks MCP.
6.lacks: No attack library, multi-turn simulation or CI/CD red team runs.

7.reason: Agent Personas set per-agent tool and permission scope. Agent Access Keys and token brokerage hide backend credentials.
7.evidence: Agents authenticate with Agent Access Keys while the gateway brokers backend tokens
7.has: Agent Personas, Agent Access Keys, OAuth 2.1 identity proxy and token brokerage.
7.lacks: No cryptographic per-agent identity such as SPIFFE. No NHI discovery of service accounts.

8.reason: No model, dataset or AI code scanning found. AI Gateway governs agent actions, not model files.
8.evidence: Searches: Cequence model scanning SAST code scanning AI security. Read Cequence vs Prisma AIRS comparison page.
8.lacks: No model file scanner, dataset PII or poisoning scan, or AI SAST.

notes: Scope read: Cequence AI Gateway (agent containment, Agent Personas, AI Discovery), docs.aigateway.cequence.ai, and Unified API Protection. No acquisitions or rebrand found as of 2026-10-27 (Tracxn lists none). Cequence reported a record fiscal Q4 2026 on agentic AI demand. AI Discovery needs read-only SIEM access (a Splunk setup doc exists) and reports on a schedule with 30 days of trend history. Cequence's own Prisma AIRS comparison says model scanning, red teaming and AI posture management matter less when an org uses standard models, and it lists none of them as products. Unified API Protection (API Spyder, API discovery, API security testing) covers APIs, not AI assets, so it earns no AI module credit. Sensitive data detection runs on live MCP, API, LLM and A2A traffic, not on training or RAG datasets. Less sure: 7.1 (Agent Access Keys may count as a per-agent credential), 3.2 (SIEM names come from docs, remediation is agent throttle or halt), 4.1 (LLM registry docs list Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor and SDKs).
